sources.title: Longest non-repeating substring deterministic Java fixture

claims.text: The repository source explicitly requires finding the longest substring without repeated characters and returning the substring itself rather than only its length. Programming language, null behavior, Unicode unit, and equal-length tie-breaking are not preserved source requirements.

Under the explicitly labeled Java reference contract using Unicode code points and leftmost tie-breaking, the sliding-window implementation returns the same substring as an independent O(n^2) oracle for nine fixed boundary cases and 21,845 exhaustive bounded inputs over a four-symbol alphabet including a supplementary Unicode code point.

The shown implementation converts the String to a code-point array once and advances both sliding-window boundaries monotonically, giving O(n) time and O(n) worst-case auxiliary space for the array plus last-seen map; this is derived from the reference implementation rather than an unstated source constraint.
